newsitem.title: GERMANY: About 100,000 workers take part in Daimler protest.
newsitem.headline: About 100,000 workers take part in Daimler protest.

text.p: About 100,000 workers of German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG will have participated by Tuesday night in a protest day against sick-pay cuts, the Daimler-Benz works council said on Tuesday.

Karl Feuerstein, the chairman of the group's works council, said the protests had taken place at more than 50 Daimler work sites around Germany and had included participation from Daimler's DASA aerospace and debis information system units.
"Daimler-Benz management did not reckon with the reaction of the workforce and with the fact that a number of carmakers would not accompany it (in making the cuts)," Feuerstein said.
Feuerstein said he had received information from carmaker rivals Volkswagen AG, BMW AG and Porsche that they would not make the cuts in existing pacts.
He said at the demonstration held earlier at a Mercedes plant in Stuttgart that all of the approximately 10,000 workers that took part then went home for the day.
